transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

That uneven heating is likely because the plate isn't rotating, which stops the heat from spreading evenly. The most common cause is simply that the glass tray hasn’t been seated correctly on its drive coupler or something is catching it. It could also be a worn roller ring or a broken plastic coupler underneath. Please switch off and unplug the microwave, then lift out the glass plate to check if the small three-pronged coupler in the centre is cracked or loose. Refit the tray so its grooves sit firmly on that coupler and ensure nothing is touching the sides before trying it again.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
ok i took the plate out, the little plastic piece in the middle has a crack and the hole in it looks rounded. also the plate wobbles when i put it back. is that the problem?

Yes, that cracked and rounded coupler is almost certainly the problem causing the wobble and lack of rotation. Since you have confirmed the part is damaged, we need to order a replacement turntable coupler for your specific model. Could you please tell me the make and model number of your microwave? This information is usually found on a label on the back or inside the door frame. If you cannot reach that label right now, we can wait until you are able to check it.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Sharp R272WM, found it on the label at the back

[Heading: Likely cause: turntable coupler]
That suggests the cracked coupler is why your plate isn't turning properly. I've checked our database for the Sharp R272WM, but we couldn't find a specific match for its turntable parts. To get you sorted with the right replacement, I'd suggest contacting Sharp's official spare parts service or booking an engineer who can supply and fit the correct coupler. This ensures you get a part that fits perfectly and keeps your microwave safe to use.
